text: Conditional Split works exactly like a CASE decision structure: it evaluates one or more expressions per row, and routes each row down to its first genuinely matching stream, with an optional default stream catching anything that matches nothing at all.

A real example: split year less than nineteen sixty into one stream, year greater than nineteen eighty into another, with everything else falling into a default stream. Disjoint controls whether a row goes to only its first match, the common case, or to every single stream it actually matches at once.

Pivot is an aggregation transformation that turns the unique values of one column into a whole set of brand-new columns. Three real inputs configure it: group by, for which columns collapse multiple rows into one; the pivot key, whose unique values become new columns; and an aggregate function generating each pivoted column's actual value.

Because pivoted column names often get generated dynamically at run time, they don't always show up automatically in Inspect or Sink mapping — enable Allow schema drift on the sink to still write them through successfully.

Unpivot does exactly the reverse of Pivot. It takes several columns and collapses them down into two — one holding what used to be the column name, one holding what used to be that column's value. Where Pivot turns a long, tidy table into a wide summary, Unpivot turns a wide table back into a long, tidy one a downstream aggregation can actually work with.
